resources.string: The right time for every task
What Kairos does, the priority score, the version
Kairos ranks your tasks for the day and fits them into the gaps of your calendar, at the right time.
It ranks the day’s tasks by a priority score, shown on each one.
It fits each task into the gaps of the calendar, around meetings, with a buffer after each meeting.
It protects deep-work blocks and lightens the afternoon slump.
It tracks the time actually spent and compares it with the estimate.

Value grows fourfold with each priority step (P0 is worth 4 times P1), the deadline weighs more and more as it approaches, and effort is measured in Fibonacci points. Small and important goes before big and distant. An overdue task always goes first.
In Greek, kairos means the opportune moment, the right instant to act, as opposed to chronos, time passing by. That is the tool’s job: finding the right slot for each task.

What Kairos is for and what it does
Six steps to get started with Kairos
Members, backlog, tracking, forecasts and exchanges
Jot down an idea, a to-do, a message here, without thinking. Later, turn a note into a task: it lands in the Day view, to be processed.
“Up next” tells you what to do. Tasks to process are waiting for their priority, points and deadline; the score (value divided by effort) sets the order. Start the timer to measure real time.

The seven days of the week: deadlines, finished tasks, time slots and real time. “Month” shows the whole month: planned tasks, deadlines, overloaded days, public holidays and days off. Tap a day to open it in the Day view.
What you really do: throughput, time spent by task type, and the calibration of your estimates (your points against real time).
Settings are grouped by category: general, day and hours, planning, timer and statistics, team, data. A change is kept from one category to the next until you press “Save” at the bottom.
Team tracking: who does what, progress and signals (delays, blockers, unestimated tasks). Tap a task to see its details, reassign it or enter its progress.
The team’s tasks: create them here, qualify them (priority, points, category, deadline), then assign them to a member, or ask for a suggested split.
The members, their capacity and their load over the chosen horizon. Tap a member for their sheet (absences, activity). The “Exchanges” tab sends tasks and receives progress by file.
A member who uses Kairos receives their tasks in a file and sends you their progress in another. No server: pass the files along however you like.
The probability of meeting a deadline and the likely finish date, by simulation. “What if…?” compares scenarios without touching the real tasks.

Too many tasks, not enough time: the hardest part is knowing which one to start with. Kairos decides the order for you (each task’s value divided by its effort), fits it into the gaps of your calendar and measures what you really do. Your data stays on your device: no account, no network.
An idea, a to-do, a message: jot it down in a second in Notes, turn it into a task later.
Priority, effort points, deadline: in a few clicks, Kairos derives a score.
The Day view shows what to do now, in order, around your meetings and your deep work.
A timer per task, alerts, and real time compared with your estimate.
The seven days at a glance: deadlines, finished tasks, time slots.
Throughput, time by task type and the calibration of your estimates.
You lead a team? Turn on team management (Settings → Team): members, backlog, load, forecasts and progress tracking.
You work for a manager? Import the file they send you (Settings → Data → Import), then send your progress back. No server: you pass the files along however you like.
In Notes, write down whatever comes to mind, without sorting. A note becomes a task whenever you want.
A task to process is waiting for its priority, effort points and deadline. “How to qualify?” helps you choose; Kairos derives a score.
“Up next” shows the task to do, the next ones are ranked by score around your meetings. “Why this position?” explains each rank.
Start the timer on a task: Kairos measures real time, warns you when you go over and compares it with your estimate.
The Week shows the seven days at a glance. The statistics compare estimated and real time to sharpen your estimates.
Export your data regularly (Settings → Data). Received a file from your manager? Import it in the same place, then “Send back progress…”. Leading a team? Turn it on in Settings → Team.
Add the team’s members: availability, hours per day, absences. “This is me” links your sheet to your Personal space.
Create the team’s tasks and qualify them: priority, points, category, deadline. The score ranks them.
Assign each task to a member, or ask for a suggested split based on everyone’s load.
The board shows everyone’s status and the signals: delays, blockers, unestimated tasks. Every change is recorded in the log.
Simulate the end of the work: dates as percentages of chance, threatened deadlines, “What if…?” scenarios without touching the real tasks.
A member uses Kairos? In the “Exchanges” tab of the Team screen, send them their tasks; they send back a progress file that you integrate. Otherwise, enter progress in Tracking.
Send a member their tasks: Kairos saves a file, for you to pass along however you like (email, messaging, USB stick, shared folder).
They open it with “Import” (Settings → Data), work in their Kairos, then choose “Send back progress…”.
They pass you their report: receive it here. A preview shows what will change before you integrate it.
Progress shows up in Tracking. A member without Kairos? Enter their progress by hand in Tracking.
The files are not encrypted: they contain the titles and descriptions of the tasks.

Kairos walks you through the task sheet, field by field, then shows where your task lands in the day.
Priority (P0 to P3) says how much it matters, points (Fibonacci) how big it is, minutes how long it takes. The points guide shows tasks you already finished.
Each task gets a score: its value divided by its effort. Tasks are laid into the gaps of the day, and the afternoon dip keeps heavy ones out of your low hours. “Why this position?” explains it.
Hours by day of the week
In Settings, each day can keep the usual working day, have its own hours, or be a day off where nothing is scheduled automatically.
A task without an estimate takes the median real time of its last timed occurrences. It shows as ~45 min, and an estimate you type always wins.
Seven days at a glance: deadlines, scheduled tasks, finished tasks and slots. Open a day to see its agenda.
Split a task into subtasks: only the leaves are scheduled, and the parent shows its progress. You can rename them from the task’s sheet.
A task can come back daily, on weekdays, weekly or monthly. “Snooze” sends it to the next working day, and “Move…” picks any day.
Say which task waits for which: a blocked task leaves the agenda until its blocker is done, and the critical path comes first.
Add meetings and breaks as busy slots, or reserve a deep work slot: Kairos puts your most urgent task in it and plans around the rest.
Plain settings, defaults one tap away
Settings speak plainly, with the language and the theme color first, and “Restore default settings” brings every value back.
A guided walk through the task sheet
A title that states the expected result (“Ship the PDF export”), then what is needed to get started. This is what the assignee will read in their pack.
Leave “Unassigned” to put it in the Backlog, or pick a member: the menu shows their load. The effort counts for them as soon as you save; you can reassign it later, and the log will keep track.

Priority orders the Backlog and Tracking (P0 in red). Points give the relative size: without an estimate, the effort comes from the real median of tasks of the same size, otherwise from the hours per point in Settings.

An estimate in minutes wins over points: it is the effort that load and forecasts use (the “Effort” line says where it comes from). The deadline feeds the Tracking signals and the probability of meeting it.
The category is the task type: load and forecasts can also be read by category, and real durations per category refine the estimates.
A team task can only wait for another team task. If it repeats, its next occurrence keeps the assignee. The rest (project, fixed time, subtasks) works as in the Personal space.
It lands in the Backlog, or “To do” with its assignee. Then: “Start” moves it to “In progress”, progress is set in the sheet, and the “History” tab keeps every step.
Step by step: assignee, size, effort, category.
Step by step: the rule, the first date and the next ones.
Set up Kairos step by step
Working day, hours, contexts, best hours: one card at a time.
A recurring task is an ordinary task that comes back. Give it a stable title, a verb and a result: “Collect the mail”, “Pay the rent”.
The rule starts from the deadline: it is the first occurrence, and the next ones count from it. Without a deadline, Kairos starts from today.

Pick the rule in “Repeat”. Daily, weekdays, weekly and monthly come back when you finish an occurrence; weekdays skips weekends and the holidays of your settings. “On day N of the month” is created every month, done or not, and moves back to the previous working day.
Priority, points and minutes apply to every occurrence. Without minutes, Kairos learns the duration of the series as you time it.
Press Save: the first occurrence is created. Finishing an occurrence creates the next one. Nothing is written before.

The start and end of your day bound the plan; the default duration places a task without an estimate, the buffer gives you a breather after a busy slot.
Nothing is written during the tour. Press Save to keep your changes, or Discard changes to go back.
“%1$s” is in the Backlog: assign it when someone can take it.

Title: a verb and a result
Name the task with a verb and the expected result (“Send the quote to Marc”). It is the only field you have to fill in.
Add the context, a link or a list you would otherwise forget. Leave it empty when the title says it all.
P0 is critical, P3 can wait. Red is reserved for P0, so keep it rare: if everything is P0, nothing is.

Pick a size (1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21), not a duration. The Fibonacci sequence spreads the values out because the bigger a task is, the less precisely we can guess it. The guide below shows tasks you already finished.
Optional. Without it, Kairos takes the duration of your points, then the default duration of the Settings. After a few timed occurrences it can suggest the real duration.
The deadline raises the score as it gets close. “Scheduled for”, in the more options, keeps the task for the day you can start it.
The type groups your statistics and can suggest a duration. Types are managed in the Settings.
Project, fixed time, recurrence, subtasks and blockers are here. You can come back to them later from the task’s sheet.
Press Save: the task is created and placed in your day. Nothing is written before.
The score ranks your tasks: value divided by effort. Tap the score to read “Why this position?”.
This task is not in today’s agenda: it waits in “To process” until it has a priority and points, or in “Later” if its day is not today.
Kairos lays the task into a gap of the day, with its duration. The timeline shows where, among your slots and pinned tasks.
The tick finishes the task, ▷ starts the timer, “Snooze” moves it to the next working day and the pencil edits it. Priority, points, duration and deadline are shown on the row.
Well done: it is in your day, ranked by Kairos. Do things in order, and the next ones take seconds.
Show me where it is placed
Your day only holds examples. Kairos can walk you through a real task, field by field.
Chapters on every feature, reopened whenever you like from Settings, from help or from the home page, and a “New in this version” section.
The guide remembers and shows the spot
Chapters you finish are marked as read, “Hide” keeps the news hidden until the next version, and “Show me the screen” opens the exact section, highlighted.
Move a task from the week
Tap a task in the Week view to schedule it on another day; public holidays and days off are flagged, and “Undo” brings back its date.
Narrow the statistics by period (4, 8, 12 weeks or all) and with the Day view’s filters, then export the tables as CSV or a card as an image.
A recurring “weekdays” time slot, like the daily stand-up, no longer lands on a public holiday or on an extra day off set in Settings.
Monthly slots, and one day apart
A time slot can come back every month, on the 15th or on the 3rd Tuesday. On a recurring slot, “Only this one” skips that day or changes its hours, without touching the rest of the series.
Import your meetings from a calendar

Settings → Data → Calendars imports an .ics file from Outlook, Google Calendar or Thunderbird: each meeting becomes a busy slot, whole-day events a badge on the day. Import it again to update it. On Android, the phone’s calendars can also be read live.
A copy of your data in a synced folder

On the desktop and Android, Settings → Data → “Create a file” keeps an up-to-date copy of your data in a folder you choose (Syncthing, Nextcloud…). If another device changed it, Kairos asks before writing.
In the Week view, “Month” shows every day of the month: planned tasks, deadlines, overloaded days, public holidays and days off. Tap a day to open it.
In Statistics, “Correct the estimates…” replaces the estimate of finished tasks with the timed duration, after a preview where you untick what to keep; “Undo” brings the old ones back.
Statistics show the tracked time day by day and the estimation bias week by week, each chart with its written summary.
Statistics tell at which hour you finish each type fastest compared with your estimates. Settings → Best hours can use it: Measure by Efficiency, or Both.
Recurring task and Settings, step by step
In “Discover Kairos”: “Create my first recurring task” shows the next deadline of each rule; “Set up Kairos step by step” goes through the Settings one card at a time and saves nothing before “Save”.

Call the priorities and the points in your own words (“Urgent”, S/M/L…). The badge shows your name, the sheet and the guide show it with its value (“M (3)”); P0 stays red and Kairos still computes with the values.
In Settings → Timer and statistics, reminders warn you before a fixed-time task and, if you want, when the plan moves on to the next task. Off by default.
General, Day and hours, Planning, Timer and statistics…: each category has its icon and summary; on a wide screen, the list and the category sit side by side.
Kairos follows your system’s theme. The “Dark theme” switch in Appearance picks the other one; switching it back follows the system again.

Kairos speaks English, French, Spanish, German, Russian and Italian. It follows your system language when it is one of these (English otherwise); Settings → General → Language picks another one. Dates, hours and numbers follow it.
A context groups task types (Work, Home…). A window reserved for a context only takes its tasks; a task with no context goes in any window. Days left “As usual” stay open to everything.
Add task types in “Task types” to put them in a context.
In Settings, give a day several working windows (morning, evening…) and reserve a window for a context such as Work or Home, which groups task types. A task only goes in a window of its context.

When you work on each type
Statistics now show, for each type of task, the 2-hour slots where you really work, compared with your usual rhythm. This card only observes: your plan uses it only if you turn it on in Settings.

Kairos can prefer, between tasks of similar score, the hours when you usually work each task type (measured from your timer, see Statistics). Off by default; overdue tasks and urgency always come first.
Frequency: the hours when you work this type. Efficiency: those when you finish it faster than estimated (needs estimates).
Leave empty to use the detected hours. A preferred hour wins over detection and works without any timer history.
Add task types in “Task types” to give them a preferred hour.
Placed here because you usually work “%1$s” tasks around this time (see Statistics). A soft preference only: urgency and overdue tasks come first.
Placed here because you set a preferred hour for “%1$s”. A soft preference only: urgency and overdue tasks come first.
Placed here because you usually finish “%1$s” tasks faster than estimated around this time (see Statistics). A soft preference only: urgency and overdue tasks come first.
Placed here because you often work “%1$s” tasks around this time and finish them faster than estimated (see Statistics). A soft preference only: urgency and overdue tasks come first.

In Settings, turn on “Prefer my usual hours”: between tasks of similar score, Kairos picks the one whose type you usually work at that time, or at the hour you set for it. Overdue tasks and urgency still come first.
